reframings.assumptions_changed: The assumption that automated systems lack any form of rigorous self-correction has been challenged by the existence of automated falsification agents (Popper) and optimized simulation testing.
reframings.new_frame: Automated systems can effectively perform hypothesis-level falsification within predefined frameworks, but these mechanisms do not extend to autonomous revision of foundational methodological assumptions.
reframings.old_frame: Automated decision-making systems lack external auditing mechanisms for high-stakes tasks.
reframings.reason: New evidence demonstrates that while tactical falsification is becoming automated, the foundational assumptions remain exogenous or fixed in the design phase.
reframings.strategy: Distinguish between tactical falsification (the 'what' of the data) and strategic epistemic correction (the 'why' of the method).
reframings.trigger: Review of Popper and BO evidence.
